name: Prananadeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Thirumangalakudi near Kumbakonam with a five-tiered gopuram, counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams hymned by Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar. It is one of the few places in South India where the Kaali Attam dance is performed, and its goddess Mangalambigai is invoked for the welfare of married women.
story: A minister of Kulothunga Chola, executed for building the temple with tax money, is said to have revived here through Mangalambigai's grace when his funeral bier reached the shrine.

name: Agniswarar Temple
significance: Shiva temple northeast of Kumbakonam revered in Appar's Tevaram and counted among the nine Navagraha temples of Tamil Nadu as the shrine of Sukra (Venus), whom devotees propitiate here against the planet's malefic effects. Built by the medieval Cholas and renovated under Vijayanagar, it has a five-tiered rajagopuram and two prakarams.
story: Shiva is said to have blessed the sage Parasara with a vision of his cosmic dance at this place, and Sukra is believed to reside within the body of the presiding deity.

name: Dayanidheeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva shrine on the Kaveri in Thanjavur district praised by Sambandar in the Tevaram, and one of the 88 temples of the Thanjavur Palace Devasthanam administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department.
story: Hanuman, travelling south along the Kaveri with Rama, is said to have installed the Dayanidhi lingam here, giving the village its name, "the river-forest of the northern monkey".

name: Karkadeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the early medieval Tevaram by Tirugnanasambandar; the shrine near Thiruvisanallur is known as the "crab temple" (karkadam) from its founding legend.
story: A gandharva cursed by Durvasa to live as a crab worshipped the lingam here, and when Indra struck at it a hole opened in the lingam to shelter the creature.

name: Satyagireeswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam at Senganur (Seynjalur) glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram and mentioned in Sekkizhar's Periyapuranam; it is also counted among the seven Saptha Vigraha shrines arrayed around the Mahalingaswamy temple of Thiruvidaimarudur.

name: Apathsahayar Temple
significance: Reckoned among the earliest Chola temples, this Paadal Petra Sthalam near Thiruvaiyaru is revered in the 7th-century Tevaram and belongs to the Saptha Sthanam group of shrines; its masonry spans the 9th-century Cholas to 16th-century Nayak and Vijayanagar additions.
story: When the son of the devotee Apoothi Adigal died of snakebite while cutting plantain leaves for Appar, the saint's prayer to Apathsahayar ("helper in danger") restored the boy to life.

name: Aiyarappar Temple
significance: The great Shiva temple of Thiruvaiyaru, "the place of five rivers", a Paadal Petra Sthalam revered by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, spreading over some 60,000 square metres with four gopurams and five prakarams. Chola queens added the Uttarakailasam and Dakshinakailasam shrines, and Nayak-era work extended the complex to the 16th century.
story: Nandi is believed to have been born here to the sage Salandha and bathed by five sacred waters, and Appar is said to have been granted a vision of Mount Kailasa at this shrine.

name: Neyyadiappar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Thiruvaiyaru revered in the Tevaram and counted among the seven Saptha Sthanam temples of the Aiyarappar circuit. Built by Aditya Chola I in the 9th century, it preserves an inscription of AD 862 from the reign of the Pandya king Marajadaiyan.
story: A cow poured its ghee daily over a buried lingam; when the spot was dug up the lingam was found and the lord was named Neyyadiappar, "the lord bathed in ghee".

name: Vyakrapureeswarar Temple
significance: A north-bank Kaveri shrine in Thanjavur district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar, and counted among the Nava Puliyur ("nine tiger-town") temples associated with the sages Patanjali and Vyaghrapada.

name: Vaidyanathaswami Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam on the north bank of the Kaveri in Ariyalur district, glorified in the Tevaram; it is famed for its annual wedding festival of Nandikesvarar and houses the largest bronze statue of the poet-saint Thiruvalluvar in Tamil Nadu, cast from 750 kg of metal.

name: Alanduraiyar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam at Kilpaluvur in Ariyalur district associated with the 7th-century saint Tirugnanasambandar; the ancient brick shrine was rebuilt in stone during the reigns of Parantaka Chola II and Uttama Chola.
story: Parasurama is believed to have worshipped here to be rid of the sin of slaying his mother.

name: Semmeninathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams built on the northern bank of the Kaveri in Thanjavur district, glorified in the Tevaram hymns of Tirugnanasambandar and Tirunavukkarasar (Appar).

name: Sathyavaheesvarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam on the banks of the Kollidam near Lalgudi, venerated in the Tevaram of Sambandar and Appar; the temple, attributed to Parantaka Chola I, has a five-tiered gopuram, three prakarams and notable images of Dakshinamurthy and Brahma.
story: When floods kept the boy-saint Sambandar on the far bank, Ganesha bent forward to hear his hymns, earning the name Sevi Saitha Vinayagar, "the Vinayaka who lent his ear".

name: Neelivaneswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, about 20 km north of Tiruchirappalli, with a shrine ascribed to Mahendravarman I (c. 640 CE) and inscriptions of Rajaraja I and Rajendra I. Known as Thenkailasam, it draws unmarried devotees seeking spouses and preserves a venerated plantain tree and Rathina Sabha.
story: In a contest of strength between Vayu and Adisesha, eight fragments of Mount Kailasa were scattered across the south, and Thiruppainjeeli's white hill (Suwethagiri) is held to be one of them.

name: Mattrurai Varadeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, at Thiruvasi near Tiruchirappalli, celebrated in the Tevaram hymns of Tirugnanasambandar and Sundarar; the site was anciently known as Tirupachilasramam.

name: Jambukeswarar Temple, Thiruvanaikaval
significance: One of the five Pancha Bhoota Sthalams of Shiva, embodying the element water — an underground stream keeps the sanctum lingam perpetually wet — and also a Paadal Petra Sthalam. The vast complex carries 11th–12th-century Chola inscriptions and was greatly expanded, with its seven-tiered rajagopuram, by the Hoysala king Someswara in 1236–37.
story: Parvati, doing penance on earth, fashioned a lingam of water beneath a jambu tree, where two cursed celestials worshipped it as an elephant and a spider until their devotion freed them.

name: Maragadachaleswarar Temple
significance: A hilltop Paadal Petra Sthalam above the Kaveri in Tiruchirappalli district, glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram, and counted among the eight sites believed to hold fragments of Mount Kailasa.
story: A trial of strength between Vayu and Adisesha is said to have hurled eight pieces of Kailasa southward, one of which became the hill of Thiruengoimalai.

name: Abathsahayeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, at Ponnur in Mayiladuthurai district, celebrated in the Tevaram poetry of Tirugnanasambandar and Tirunavukkarasar.

name: Amravaneswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Tiruchirappalli glorified by Appar and Sambandar and expanded by 11th-century Chola kings, whose inscriptions line its walls. It is known as a Moola Nakshatra parihara shrine where those born under the Moola star pray for marriage.
story: Shiva is said to have fed a mango to a deer here under the sacred mango tree — maan (deer) giving the village its name Manthurai.

name: Parasunathar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Muzhaiyur near the old Chola capital of Pazhayarai, mentioned by the saint Appar and counted among the Vaippu Sthalams of the Tevaram; besides the shivalinga it houses images of Parashurama, Murugan and Vinayaka.

name: Manickavannar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, at Tiruvalaputhur in Mayiladuthurai district, glorified in the early medieval Tevaram poems of Tirugnanasambandar and Sundarar.

name: Kundala Karaneswarar Temple
significance: The 28th Tevara Paadal Petra Sthalam of Chola Nadu north of the Kaveri, near Vaitheeswaran Koil; it is one of the very few shrines where Hanuman is depicted worshipping Shiva.
story: Hanuman is said to have offered his kundalams (earrings) to Shiva here, giving the deity the name Kundala Karaneswarar.

name: Pasupatiswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam revered in Sambandar's Tevaram, with 11th-century Chola masonry and inscriptions running from Rajaraja I to Rajaraja III; its white lingam bears the mark of a cow's hoof, and the complex includes a five-tiered rajagopuram and three prakarams.
story: Parvati, cursed to become the cow Kamadhenu for delaying the sunset at play, worshipped Shiva over a snake's lair at Pandanallur until he released her.

name: Palunkanda Nathar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Thiruvaipadi near Thiruppanandal, praised by Tirunavukkarasar in the Tevaram and closely tied to the life of Chandeshvara Nayanar, one of the 63 Nayanmars.
story: The cowherd boy Chandesvara raised a shivalinga of sand here and bathed it daily with the milk of his herd, a devotion that won him sainthood.

name: Vilwaneswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam north of Kumbakonam on the Kollidam's southern side, revered in the Tevaram by Appar, Sundarar and Sambandar; the temple has a five-tiered gateway tower and the Yama Theertham tank.
story: A hunter chased up a vilva tree on Shivaratri unknowingly showered its leaves on a lingam all night, and the pleased Shiva later saved him from Yama, the god of death.

name: Saptharisheeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Lalgudi (Thiruthavathurai) reckoned about 1,200 years old and sung by the saint Appar; it is celebrated for its 30-foot wooden temple chariot bearing over 2,000 carvings, among the tallest in Tamil Nadu.
story: The seven Saptarishis are said to have worshipped Shiva here and, after penance, risen into the sky as the seven stars.

name: Arunajadeswarar (Thaalapureeswarar) Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, on the Kollidam at Thiruppanandal, praised by Tirugnanasambandar, Tirunavukkarasar, Nambiyandar Nambi and later Arunagirinathar; the west-facing temple has three prakaras and shrines of Ambika, Durga and Naga Kanni.

name: Ratnagiriswarar Temple
significance: A hill temple in Karur district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, with Tevaram verses composed in its praise by Appar and Sundarar; the shrine crowns the Ratnagiri hill at Ayermalai near Kulithalai.

name: Kadambavaneswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, standing on the south bank of the Kaveri at Kulithalai in Karur district, with hymns sung in its praise by Tirunavukkarasar (Appar).
story: Shiva is said to have appeared to the sage Kanva in the kadamba forest here, whence the place was called Kadambanthurai.

name: Tharukavaneswarar (Paraithurainathar) Temple
significance: A Chola-period Paadal Petra Sthalam on the Kaveri west of Tiruchirappalli, honoured in the Tevaram of the Nayanmars; the temple has a seven-tiered gateway tower, two precincts and numerous Chola inscriptions.
story: Shiva as the mendicant Bhikshatana and Vishnu as the enchantress Mohini are said to have humbled the proud sages of the Tharuka forest at this spot.

name: Ujjeevanathar Temple (Uyyakondan Thirumalai)
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam on a 30-metre hillock above the Uyyakondan channel in Tiruchirappalli, revered in the Tevaram by Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar. Built in the Sembian Chola age around 950 CE, it bears inscriptions of Rajaraja I and Kulothunga I and was occupied by French and English troops during the 1753–54 siege of Trichinopoly.
story: When Yama came for the sixteen-year-old devotee Markandeya, Shiva burst from the lingam here, kicked Death away and left the boy sixteen forever.

name: Panchavarnaswamy Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam in Woraiyur, the ancient Chola capital within present-day Tiruchirappalli, revered in the Tevaram; its lingam is believed to show five different colours through the day, and the temple preserves eight Chola inscriptions naming Rajaraja I and Rajendra I.
story: Shiva is said to have appeared to the sage Udanga in five colours across the day, and five lingams borne by Nagaraja merged into the single image worshipped here.

name: Thayumanaswami Temple, Rockfort
significance: The Shiva temple of Tiruchirappalli's Rockfort, cut into a 273-foot monolith whose cave shrines go back to the Pallavas; the main complex was raised by the Pandyas in the 8th century and renewed by Vijayanagara and Madurai Nayak rulers. The deity is revered in the Tevaram, making it a Paadal Petra Sthalam.
story: Shiva took the form of a devotee's absent mother to deliver Rathnavathi's child during a flood, earning the name Thayumanavar, "he who became a mother".

name: Erumbeeswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam crowning a 60-foot hill near Tiruchirappalli, its present form raised by Aditya Chola I after the battle of Tirupurambiyam; the temple preserves 49 Chola inscriptions and draws tens of thousands for the full-moon girivalam circumambulation.
story: Shiva is said to have become an anthill and tilted his head so that ants could climb up and worship him — erumbu, the ant, names the lord Erumbeeswarar.

name: Nedungalanathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, near Tiruchirappalli, whose presiding deity Nedungalanathar (Nithya Sundareswarar) received ten Tevaram hymns from Tirugnanasambandar.

name: Athmanatheswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, at Thiruvalampozhil in Thanjavur district, celebrated in hymns by Tirunavukkarasar; pilgrims come seeking removal of obstacles to marriage and the blessing of children.

name: Pushpavananathar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Thiruvaiyaru and one of the Saptha Sthanam temples, revered in the Tevaram; its 9th-century Chola core grew through Vijayanagar and Nayak times, and it is noted for a seated image of Appar and a Durga standing on one leg.
story: Indra, cursed by Gautama with a thousand marks, is said to have been cleansed after worshipping here with flowers — poo — which named the lord Pushpavananathar.

name: Brahma Sira Kandeeswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Thiruvaiyaru revered in the Tevaram and counted among the eight Ashta Veeratanam temples marking Shiva's heroic deeds — here the severing of Brahma's fifth head; unusually, the complex contains a separate shrine to Brahma. Inscriptions record Chola, Thanjavur Nayak and Maratha patronage.
story: Shiva plucked off Brahma's fifth head at this place and was himself freed of the resulting sin after bathing in the temple's Kamala Pushkarani tank.

name: Odhanavaneswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam in Thanjavur district revered by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, known as Dakshina Kailasham; its 9th-century Chola masonry was extended to the 16th century with four gopurams and three precincts, with Pandya and Maratha contributions on record.
story: Shiva is said to have granted a devotee an inexhaustible vessel of food here, making the place Chotruthurai — "the refuge of rice".

name: Vedapuriswarar Temple
significance: An early Chola Paadal Petra Sthalam near Thiruvaiyaru revered by Appar and Sambandar, and one of the Saptha Sthanam temples; on set days in the month of Panguni the sun's rays fall directly on the lingam.
story: The lord is called Vazhaimadunathar because the lingam is said to have emerged from a banana tree.

name: Vasishteswarar Temple
significance: A Chola-built Paadal Petra Sthalam at Thenkudithittai near Thanjavur, hymned by Sambandar and Appar; a Chandrakanta stone in the vimana drips water on the lingam every 24 minutes, and the temple is a noted shrine of Guru (Brihaspati), who stands in a separate sanctum.
story: After the great deluge only this mound stayed above water, where Brahma and Vishnu found a lingam and worshipped it until Shiva appeared and restored their offices.

name: Alandurainathar Temple
significance: The Paadal Petra Sthalam of Pullamangai near Thanjavur, glorified by Tirugnanasambandar and counted by art historians among the four earliest surviving temples of the Chola Empire; it is celebrated for exquisite sculpture, including miniature panels narrating the Ramayana.

name: Chakravageswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam on the Kudamurutti branch of the Kaveri near Ayyampettai, honoured in Thevaram verses by Appar and Sambandar; begun under Aditya I and enlarged by 11th-century Cholas, it keeps inscriptions of Rajaraja I and Rajendra I and a rare circular two-tiered vimana. It is also counted among the seven Saptamatrika shrines.
story: Vishnu is said to have received his discus, the chakra, after worshipping at this temple, an event remembered in the village's name.
